title: What's In My Camera Bag for Travel (2026)
creator: Jonah Reyes
description:
Everything I carried for two weeks in Portugal, plus the stuff I've stopped bringing.

My kit (affiliate links through B&H - I get a small cut if you buy through them, same price for you):
Sony A7C II: https://bhpho.to/4kT9aZq
Sigma 28-70mm f/2.8: https://bhpho.to/3RmW2pK
DJI Mic 2: https://bhpho.to/4bN7xQe
Peak Design Everyday Sling 10L: https://bhpho.to/3Yu8vLc

Filmed in Lisbon and Porto. The full Portugal film drops next week.

sentences.t: What's up everybody, I just got back from two weeks in Portugal and I'm still kind of unpacking.
So I figured, while everything's still spread out on the bed, let's go through exactly what I brought.
Quick heads up before we start.
Every piece of gear in this video is linked in the description, and those are affiliate links through B&H.
That means if you buy something with them, I get a small percentage, and the price is exactly the same for you.
It's honestly one of the ways this channel pays for the next trip, so I appreciate it.
Alright, let's start with the camera, which is the Sony A7C II.
I switched to this from a much bigger body last year, and the main reason is just size.
When I'm walking around a city for ten hours, I don't want a brick hanging off my shoulder.
It fits in the sling with the lens attached, which sounds small, but it means I actually pull it out.
That's the whole game with travel footage, honestly, the best camera is the one you didn't leave in the hotel.
Lens wise, I only brought one this time.
It's the Sigma twenty-eight to seventy, the f two point eight one.
I used to bring three primes and I'd spend half the day swapping lenses on a street corner like an idiot.
This is wide enough for the little streets in Alfama and tight enough for detail shots of food and tiles and stuff.
Is it as sharp as a prime?
Probably not.
Has a single person in the comments ever noticed?
Also no.
Audio, I've got the DJI Mic 2.
Two transmitters, one receiver, and the case charges everything.
I clip one on myself for the talking bits, and the other one I'll sometimes just set on a café table to grab the ambient sound.
The internal recording backup has saved me twice now when the signal dropped behind a wall.
The bag itself is a Peak Design sling, the ten liter one.
I know people love a big backpack, but for city stuff the sling is so much better, because you swing it around and grab the camera without taking anything off.
Then the small stuff.
Three batteries, which is overkill, but I've been burned before.
Two fast SD cards, and I swap them every day, so if one dies I lose one day and not the whole trip.
A tiny tripod that doubles as a handle.
And a variable ND filter, which is the one thing beginners always skip and then wonder why their daytime footage looks so choppy.
Now, the stuff I've stopped bringing.
The gimbal is gone.
In-body stabilization plus a little warp stabilizer in post is plenty for how I shoot now.
Drone, also gone, mostly because the rules in a lot of European city centers make it more hassle than it's worth.
And the laptop, which is the big one.
I just back up to a little SSD every night and edit when I get home.
It's weirdly freeing, I actually enjoy the trip instead of editing in the hotel until two in the morning.
So yeah, that's the whole bag.
The Portugal film itself goes up next week, and I'm really happy with how it turned out.
If you've got a question about any piece of this, drop it below and I'll try to answer everyone.
See you in the next one.
